h2: Third-party quality inspection in Jacksonville: what Atlantis covers, and when you need a sorting or load-test firm
html:
Third-party quality inspection in Jacksonville: what Atlantis covers, and when you need a sorting or load-test firm

"Third party quality inspection services" covers a wide range of work in Jacksonville searches, from sorting suspect parts to load testing cranes. Atlantis does one part of it: conventional nondestructive testing, meaning UT, MT, PT and VT, on welds, plate, piping, tanks and lifting gear, performed independently of the people who built or repaired them. The list below shows where other kinds of firms fit.

Sorting, load testing and NDT are different services

  • Third-party sorting companies contain and sort suspect parts for manufacturers and their suppliers, usually by visual and gauge checks at the customer's plant. Atlantis does not provide sorting or containment.
  • Load testing of cranes, hoists, spreader beams and rigging uses test weights or water bags and a qualified person to witness and certify the lift. Load test firms do that. Atlantis can examine hooks, welds and other critical parts by MT before and after the test so cracks are found on the ground rather than under load: magnetic particle inspection of lifting equipment.
  • Steel wire rope is inspected visually by a qualified person under the ASME B30 standard that covers the equipment, and electromagnetic rope testing is a specialist service. Atlantis does not test wire rope; it can examine end fittings and welded attachments by MT or PT.
  • NDT measures wall loss and finds cracks and weld flaws, with each result tied to a location, a procedure, a certified technician and a calibrated instrument. This is Atlantis work.

Jacksonville's maritime and Navy equipment base

Jacksonville is a major Navy fleet concentration area. BAE Systems' ship repair yard on Heckscher Drive sits two miles up the St. Johns River from the Atlantic, with a 25,000-ton shiplift and two marine railways, and handles Navy ships alongside tugs, megayachts and tankers. Port terminals, fuel storage along the river and utility plants add tanks, piping and structural steel. Conventional NDT answers most of their routine questions:

  • UT thickness on hull, deck and tank plating, terminal piping and tank shells: ultrasonic testing in Jacksonville and ultrasonic testing for marine and shipbuilding
  • MT on carbon steel structural and repair welds, crane pedestals and mooring fittings: magnetic particle testing in Jacksonville
  • PT on aluminum superstructure and stainless piping: penetrant testing in Jacksonville
  • VT of welds, coating breakdown and external corrosion in humid salt air

Navy ship repair NDT follows NAVSEA technical requirements and the contract's own personnel qualification rules, so confirm what the contract demands before a scope is agreed. For thickness measurement that a class surveyor will credit, IACS rules require a firm approved by that vessel's society. Atlantis is in the process of obtaining UR Z17 approval from DNV, Lloyd's Register and ABS; until then its hull readings support owner and charterer decisions, not class credit.

Florida rules that shape the scope

Florida's Boiler Safety Act, Chapter 554 of the Florida Statutes, is carried out by the State Fire Marshal's boiler safety program under Rule 69A-51 of the Florida Administrative Code, which sets inspection requirements for boilers in public assembly locations. Terminal and plant pressure vessels are normally inspected because the owner's API 510 program, the insurer or, for covered processes, OSHA's process safety standard requires it. Atlantis supplies NDT data to the owner's inspector; it is not an authorized inspection agency and never signs as inspector of record.

Choosing a Jacksonville provider

Ask every bidder the same questions:

  • Which of the services above does this job need: sorting, load testing, NDT or a mix?
  • Which technicians will be on site, and are they certified Level II in each method under a written practice?
  • Whose ASNT Level III signature is on the procedures, and does that person also review the report?
  • For Navy, class or insurer work, does the end customer accept this company's personnel certification?
  • When will the report be issued? Agree the date before mobilization.

Atlantis in Jacksonville

Atlantis is based in Houston and sends crews to Jacksonville, Mayport and the St. Johns River terminals for agreed dates, and a Level III certified by ASNT reviews each report before it is issued. Radiographs, where a specification needs them, are taken by the owner's licensed radiography contractor; Atlantis does not perform radiography in the United States.
